title: The Spark Artifact records its own unfinished bindings: most RateLimitIDs are explicitly deferred to a future iteration
content:
The `Rate Limit IDs` slot is the one place where the template is mostly unpopulated. USDC (A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.3.1.1.2.2.3), Dai (.1.3.2.3), USDT (.1.4.2.3), pyUSD (.1.5.2.3) and Aave Prime USDS (.2.1.2.3) all carry the same sentence: "The specific `RateLimitID`(s) for this conduit's inflow and outflow will be specified in a future iteration of the Spark Artifact." The Aave `Pool` parameter (.2.1.2.2.3) is deferred the same way.

Only the wETH instance (A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.3.1.1.6.2.3.1/.2) publishes actual identifiers — a 32-byte inflow hash and a distinct outflow hash.

What is missing matters more than it first appears. The RateLimitID is the key under which an on-chain limit is stored; without it, the Artifact states the *values* of a limit but not *which deployed limit* those values correspond to. Verifying that the documented 100,000,000 USDC inflow cap matches the live contract state therefore requires out-of-band knowledge, breaking the audit chain from governance text to chain state for all but one instance.

The honesty is itself a pattern: rather than omitting the slot or asserting a value it does not have, the Artifact publishes a named placeholder with a commitment to fill it. That makes the gap enumerable and reviewable — a deliberate trade of completeness for traceability — but it also means an `Active` instance can be fully operational while its documentation is not yet independently verifiable.
description: Only the wETH instance publishes concrete inflow/outflow RateLimitID hashes; USDC, Dai, USDT, pyUSD and Aave Prime USDS all state the identifiers will be specified later, leaving doc-to-chain
